source_text:
ζητεῖν προσεδόκων γὰρ ἀπὸ Κύπρου ἀποστέλλεσθαι, νῦν οὖν ὅπερ εὗρον ἀπέστειλα.
καταξίωσον οὖν κελεῦσαι τῷ πρεσβυτέρῳ τῆς παροικίας δέξασθαι παρὰ τοῦ
ἀναγνώστου τὸ ἀπεσταλμένον, καὶ παρακαλῶ πρόσταξον ἵνα μὴ τοιαῦτα ἁπλοῦται
ἐν ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις· πρέπει γὰρ τῇ σῇ τιμιότητι περὶ πάντων φροντίζειν καὶ
ἀκριβολογεῖν περὶ τῶν συμφερόντων τῇ τοῦ θεοῦ ἐκκλησίᾳ καὶ τοῖς λαοῖς τοῖς
ἐμπεπιστευμένοις σοι.
thought_title: Sending the replacement curtain and urging John to prevent such hangings
orientation: Epiphanius is closing his letter to John of Jerusalem, explaining that he has now sent the replacement curtain and asking John to order the local presbyter to receive it and to prevent such images in churches.
pass_a_gloss: For I was expecting it to be sent from Cyprus, so now I have sent what I found. Deign therefore to order the presbyter of the parish to receive from the reader what has been sent, and I urge you to command that such things not be hung in the churches; for it is fitting for your honor to care about all things and to examine carefully the things that are beneficial to the church of God and to the peoples entrusted to you.

choices.why: The verb carries a sense of condescension or graciousness fitting a bishop's request to a fellow bishop; 'deign' preserves the formal, honorific register.
The glossary does not cover these terms, but 'presbyter' is the standard rendering for the office, and 'parish' for παροικία reflects the local church community.
The verb means to spread out or unfold; in the context of curtains in churches, 'be hung' is the natural English idiom.
The glossary mandates 'honor' for τιμιότης as a title of address.
The verb means to be precise or exact in speech or inquiry; 'examine carefully' captures the sense of diligent scrutiny.
The perfect passive participle of ἐμπιστεύω means 'entrusted to'; the rendering keeps the passive force and the sense of pastoral responsibility.

pass_b_english: I had expected to send one from Cyprus, but now I have sent what I found. Deign, then, to order the presbyter of the parish to receive what has been sent from the reader, and I ask you to command that such things not be hung in the churches. For it is fitting for your honor to care about all things and to examine carefully what is beneficial for the church of God and for the people entrusted to you.

problems.why: 'λαοῖς' here means 'people' singular (the flock), not 'peoples' plural/ethnic.
problems.ruling: τοῖς λαοῖς is plural of λαός 'people' (flock), not 'peoples' (ethnic groups); 'peoples' misleads readers.

edits.old: for the peoples entrusted to you
edits.new: for the people entrusted to you

last_rejected.fix: to be exact about what is beneficial
last_rejected.ruling: ἀκριβολογεῖν means to inquire carefully/examine precisely; 'examine carefully' is within normal range.
